title: Orchid Logistics - Eviction Waves Postmortem and Hardening Plan
summary: Postmortem of repeated GPU eviction waves during peak batch inference causing long-tail tail latency and degraded throughput. Agreed short-term mitigations (autoscale tuning, eviction-aware routing), artifacts to share, and a 30-day hardening plan with a pilot on Dedicated capacity plus runbook updates.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Recording: yes

Attendees:
- James Porter (AE, Redwood)
- Maya Chen (SE, Redwood)
- Ravi Patel (CSM, Redwood)
- Liam Reyes (Head of Platform, Orchid Logistics)
- Priya Kapoor (SRE, Orchid Logistics)
- Nora Kim (CTO, Orchid Logistics)
- Marco Silva (Ops, Orchid Logistics)

Quick summary (auto): Postmortem of multiple eviction waves on Friday impacting Orchid's night-batch scoring pipeline. Discussed root cause hypotheses (preemption + cold KV cache), short-term mitigations, and a 30-day hardening plan including pilot on Dedicated capacity.

Topics covered: see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] James (Redwood): "Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick roll call? We have, ah, Orchid on the call?"
[00:06] Liam (Orchid): "Yeah this is Liam, Priya, Nora and Marco are here as well."
[00:10] James: "Great. I'm James Porter, AE on the account, with Maya our SE and Ravi CSM. We pulled this sync to walk through the eviction waves from Friday night and lock in steps. Maya, do you want to start with the timeline?"
[00:25] Maya (Redwood SE): "Sure. So I looked through the telemetry you sent, the initial thing — there were two big spikes in preemption at 23:12 and 23:45 UTC, right in the middle of your 11pm bulk scoring run. We saw GPU pods get OOM or node-preempted, the autoscaler attempted to replenish but there was a brief period where the KV cache warmed slowly which inflated tail latency. The sequence-length histogram also shifted to much longer tails during that batch, so effective per-token compute increased.
[01:10] Priya (Orchid SRE): "Can I stop you — when you say preempted, are you talking about cloud preemption? We use GCP preemptible GPUs for the cheaper pool, but we have a fallback zone. I thought the autoscaler moved loads onto the fallback nodes; instead we saw a thrash."
[01:25] Maya: "Yes, it appears to be preemption plus the autoscaler not returning capacity fast enough; the new pods had cold K V cache and that caused more latency which in turn kicked off more concurrent requests piling up, and eventually request timeouts. It's a storm effect, basically."
[01:40] Nora (CTO): "We also saw an uptick in 5xx around the same time. Is Redwood seeing any model-level issues or is this infra only?"
[01:47] Maya: "From the logs we got, there weren't model failures. Model inference completed, but queuing and eviction caused upstream timeouts. There's one oddity: one of the model variants returned slower under certain sequence length distributions, so fallback to smaller variant might help during an eviction burst."
[02:10] Marco (Ops): "We have an ops question: our current policy uses aggressive bin-packing to save costs. Could that be causing more VMs to be preempted simultaneously?"
[02:18] James: "Yes that's consistent. Lower cost bin-packing leads to higher single-point failure during preemption windows. You trade cost for fragility. We can present a cost/latency delta chart, that's what Maya's benchmark will capture."
[02:35] Liam: "We need to understand the SLA exposure. We had business alerts at 00:05 and it's not acceptable. What options do we have short-term?"
[02:44] Ravi (Redwood CSM): "Short-term we recommend: 1) tuning autoscaler to preemptively maintain a buffer for the nightly heavy job, 2) pinning the critical batch to Dedicated or a non-preemptible pool during the job window, 3) enabling eviction-aware routing and fallback to a smaller model variant. We also think a brief Dedicated pilot will show the latency benefit without the preemption variable."
[03:15] Priya: "About pinning: our finance team is sensitive to Dedicated costs. Can we simulate before committing?"
[03:23] Maya: "Yes — we can run a short pilot for a few hours and measure p50/p95/p99 deltas. We'll provide a benchmark sheet. Also there's a middle-ground: reserve a small reserved pool or configure a burst policy that shifts extra capacity to non-preemptible nodes for the 45-minute window."
[03:40] Nora: "We also want to ensure security controls stay intact if we move to Dedicated. The SOC two — SOC2 stuff and KMS integration, will that carry over?"
[03:49] James: "Absolutely. Dedicated supports the same KMS/HSM integrations and audit log features; we can share the SOC2 package and our KMS guide. Ravi will attach those docs after this call."
[04:02] Marco: "What's the hypothesis on the cache cold-start? How long did the KV cache warm?"
[04:08] Maya: "From the traces, cold-warm cycles were 60–90 seconds to warm the most used prefixes; during that interval the p99 jumped considerably. So if autoscaler adds N pods quickly but they need to rebuild KV caches, you get global tail latency impact until cache saturation stabilizes."
[04:32] Priya: "Is there a way to pre-warm caches?"
[04:35] Maya: "Yes — we can do proactive cache pre-warm scripts that request hot prefixes after a scale event. Redwood's runtime also supports prefix-prioritization so critical prefixes load first. We'll share a runbook snippet for that."
[04:48] Liam: "Okay, so immediate plan: we want logs and exact pod traces. James, you said you'd upload a package?"
[04:54] James: "I'll get eviction-logs.tar.gz up and a short correlation file. Expect within 48 hours. Also attaching the quick-run benchmark sheet. Maya will own the benchmark."
[05:05] [crosstalk] Priya: "One more question — there was a note about model variant fallbacks. How automatic is that?"
[05:12] Maya: "You can configure policy: e.g., if p99 > X ms, route to smaller quantized variant or lower-context model. It's not on by default for your app, but it's a config we can add if you want guarded fallbacks."
[05:26] Marco: "Will fallback change output quality for scoring? We need to limit false negatives."
[05:30] Maya: "Yes there is a tradeoff; part of the pilot will quantify degradation vs latency improvement. We can tie that to an eval set you provide to measure quality delta."
[05:45] Nora: "On the security side, we'll need KMS key rotation details and access controls. Can you also provide audit log retention options?"
[05:52] James: "Yes, Ravi will add the SOC2 and audit retention appendix. We have multi-tenant audit logs and you can request longer retention as an add-on."
[06:03] [00:06:03] Liam: "Can we talk timeline? We have Black Freight in three weeks, so we need mitigations earlier."
[06:08] Ravi: "Understood. We propose: immediate mitigations (autoscale buffer + fallback config) within 3–5 days, Dedicated pilot within 7–10 days, and runbook/monitoring changes rolled in 14–30 days. That fits a 30-day hardening window before Black Freight."
[06:26] Priya: "One technical nit — the logs show repeated GKE node preemptions at the same zone. Could this be a cloud-level scheduling event?"
[06:34] Maya: "Possible — our SE team will correlate cloud provider preemption windows with Kubernetes events and autoscaler actions. If it's provider noise, we can route night jobs away from susceptible zones."
[06:46] Marco: "Also, are we sure it's not a batch request pattern? On Friday we had a spike of longer chit-chat sequences at midnight."
[06:53] Maya: "Yes. Sequence-length drift correlated: your average sequence length shifted from 32 tokens to 190 tokens in the heavy job, that's a big multiplier on per-request compute. We'll show charts in the bench."
[07:10] Liam: "Do you recommend quantization profiles as a medium-term cost control?"
[07:14] Maya: "Yes — quantized model variants can reduce per-token cost and memory, which indirectly reduces eviction risk. But quality impact must be validated on your eval set."
[07:24] Nora: "Any immediate config change we can do tonight?"
[07:27] James: "If you can allow a small non-preemptible buffer in the autoscaler for the 11pm job tonight, that would likely reduce risk. Priya, can ops change the node pool policy for a one-off?"
[07:35] Priya: "We can, but it requires a ticket and approvals. We can do it, though, if we fast-track finance approval."
[07:44] [07:44] Marco: "Ok we'll try to approve budget for the 1–2 node non-preemptible buffer tonight and confirm to James."
[07:50] Maya: "I'll also prepare a runbook section: detection rule (if p99 > X for Y minutes): 1) increase buffer, 2) enable fallback routing, 3) trigger cache pre-warm. We'll share the draft."
[08:05] James: "Let's capture responsibilities for the runbook edit. Liam/Priya will validate and accept; Maya will push the draft; Ravi will add to the SOW for the pilot."
[08:16] [small pause]
[08:20] Priya: "A few minutes ago you mentioned an odd model variant slowdown. Can you repeat?"
[08:24] Maya: "Sure. Under long sequences, one of the quantized variants had increased internal fragmentation and slower kernel paths; it's rare but visible in the traces. Fallback to a different variant or lower context window might be safer during an eviction event."
[08:40] Liam: "What about monitoring? We want alerting that ties eviction signals to business impact, not just kube events."
[08:48] Maya: "Good point — we can add synthetic probes that mimic the nightly job and surface p95/p99 tracking and degrade gracefully. We'll send a monitoring template you can plug into your alerting stack."
[09:00] Marco: "Anything else on compliance? Nora wanted to make sure the Dedicated pilot didn't change where logs live."
[09:06] James: "Logs remain under your VPC for Private/Dedicated options, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include the retention appendix."
[09:15] [longer section omitted for brevity / natural pauses and clarifications]
[40:00] Maya: "Recap: immediate actions are log upload, autoscaler buffer tonight if possible, and an initial Dedicated pilot proposal. Medium-term: pilot, quantization evaluation, runbook updates, and monitoring. Long-term: consider reserved non-preemptible capacity for night batches."
[40:18] Priya: "We'll push the finance approval tonight for a 2-node buffer and I'll upload autoscaler configs by EOD tomorrow."
[40:27] James: "We'll follow up: I'll upload correlation logs (eviction-logs.tar.gz), Maya will create bench sheet, Ravi will send SOW + SOC2 docs. Expect these by the dates in the action items."
[40:40] Liam: "Two quick questions as we close: 1) if we do the Dedicated pilot, what's the rollback plan? 2) how will we measure success?"
[40:48] Maya: "Rollback is straightforward: redirect routing back to hosted pool and decommission pilot infra. We'll keep the pilot small and start with a fraction of traffic. Success metrics: p99 reduction, throughput preservation, and no 5xxs during the job window; also quality delta under threshold on your eval set."
[41:05] Nora: "And will Redwood provide SLA credits if Dedicated fails?"
[41:10] James: "We have SLA terms for Dedicated and we can discuss escrow options in the SOW. Ravi will include that clause."
[41:18] Marco: "Ok, I think we have what we need. Any blockers?"
[41:21] Priya: "None from SRE aside from finance for tonight's node buffer, but we'll try to clear it."
[41:28] James: "Great. Last thing — artifacts I'll share immediately after the call: eviction-logs.tar.gz link (private share), benchmark template, and a short runbook draft. Please confirm receipt."
[41:40] Liam: "Will do. Thanks all."
[41:42] James: "Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the pilot kickoff — tentative follow-up next Monday same time. Ravi will send calendar invite. Bye."
[41:50] [call ends]
